clue.text: Lay trap for American president

parts.note: George Bush, and his son George W., were US presidents

explanation.surface: Someone plots to waylay a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush someone is to lie in wait and set upon them, a surprise attack from cover.

clue.text: Reduce everything to variable factor

annotationWithheld.why: 'Reduce everything to variable factor' gives ALL (everything) and Y (variable) but nothing fairly supplies the A; 'to' or 'factor' would have to give it, so a word (probably 'a') looks lost in the OCR and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Obtain money by extortion almost for every personal alarm

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: to bleed someone is to extort money from them
per means for each

explanation.surface: Being blackmailed is a cause for alarm for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from BLEED, leaving BLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager or bleeping device carried on the person to summon its wearer.

clue.text: Who pesters (without right) mixed confectionery outlet?

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred into a new order
without means leave out the letter that follows

explanation.surface: Who keeps pestering at the mixed sweets counter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without right' removes R from PESTERS, leaving PESTES; 'mixed' then rearranges WHO and PESTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling sweets and chocolates is a candy store.

clue.text: Admits drifting snow has increased

indicators.note: drifting snow moves about, so its letters are rearranged here

parts.note: something that has increased has gone up

explanation.surface: A weather report: the snowdrifts are piling higher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' looks like part of a weather picture but is the anagram signal; 'has increased' is the verb phrase meaning gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, an idiom for acknowledging a fault.

clue.text: Small island surrounded by water. Give up?

indicators.note: surrounded by means the island letter sits inside the word for water

parts.note: a wave is a body of water, standing for the sea
I is the abbreviation for island, 'small' signalling the short form

explanation.surface: Someone stranded on a tiny island wonders whether to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts I inside WAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right is to relinquish or forgo it.

clue.text: Crooned a tune, raised drink in Benidorm

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker sings, then lifts a glass in a Spanish resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIR to RIA; Benidorm is a Spanish holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit.

clue.text: Apostle's food and clothing

parts.note: St Peter was an apostle
ham is a food

explanation.surface: An apostle's meal and garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Petersham is a heavy ribbed fabric and a coat made from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham is an old-style heavy overcoat, or the corded ribbon used in hats and waistbands.

clue.text: It supports line laid down for future mole perhaps

definitions.meaning: a railway track rests on cross-beams, the line being the railway

definitions.text: laid down for future mole perhaps
definitions.meaning: a spy planted to lie dormant until activated, a mole being one example

explanation.surface: A spy is being bedded in for later work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' is a railway line, whose rails sit on wooden or concrete beams; 'laid down' then turns to espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway cross-beams carry the same name as a dormant agent who waits years before spying.

clue.text: Like Tiny — extraordinary gravitas

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests something out of its ordinary order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small person shows remarkable seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is the verb, slang DIG; 'extraordinary' rearranges TINY to NITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravitas is a weighty, serious bearing, a synonym for dignified seriousness.

clue.text: Untrustworthy but attractive person requires love nest

parts.note: a dish is slang for someone good-looking
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A handsome but shifty partner wants a love nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest means deceitful, not to be trusted.

clue.text: Pays them and is disposed to express fellow feeling

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged in a new order, so the letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone pays others and is inclined to show compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges PAYS THEM and IS; 'and' only joins the two lots of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sympathise is to share or show compassion for another's feelings.

clue.text: Runs are scarce; end of over; time for spin

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket match: runs are hard to come by, the over ends, and the spinners come on.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also builds the word a second way: 'end of over' is R, and ERA ('time') turned 'for spin' gives ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is uncommon, in short supply.

clue.text: Norm takes British title initially? Dry up!

parts.note: par is the norm or standard level, as in golf
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British honour written as initials

explanation.surface: A man named Norm accepts a knighthood and is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name but is PAR; 'initially' says the title is given by its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry up or scorch out is to make thoroughly arid.

clue.text: Force into service with media group

parts.note: the press is the news media
a gang is a group

explanation.surface: Someone is conscripted alongside a media pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressgang is to coerce, from naval gangs who seized men for service.

clue.text: The one who leads athletic club-he's a pain

parts.note: the head is the leader, as of a school
HE is taken as written, the 's a link

explanation.surface: The captain of an athletics club is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance or worry is figuratively a sore head, the idiom for a pain.

clue.text: Sprightly, magical creature: rather fanciful and unrealistic

parts.note: airy means light and lively
a fairy is a magical being

explanation.surface: A light, enchanted being is somewhat dreamy and impractical.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy describes vague, impractical ideas with no grounding.

clue.text: Piece of ground concealing quiet water tortoise

indicators.note: concealing means the ground has the quiet letter tucked away inside it

parts.note: terrain is a stretch of land
P (piano) means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A patch of land hides a silent freshwater tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts P inside TERRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which British usage calls a water tortoise.

clue.text: Uncertainty about first defensive position

indicators.note: first says this short word for about goes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning
doubt is uncertainty

explanation.surface: There is doubt about where the first fortification stood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' as the short word RE is a crossword convention, from Latin 'in the matter of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fort or strongpoint.

clue.text: Give better weapons to engineers and initially marines

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of the word and

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Engineers and marines are being re-equipped with new arms.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) and RM (Royal Marines) are British army and navy units; 'initially' takes A from 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply with fresh or improved weaponry.

clue.text: Source of liquorice flavour is restricted by American requirement

indicators.note: restricted by means the word is is hemmed in by the other letters

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: Liquorice flavouring is rationed by an American rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link verb but is fodder; 'restricted by' places it inside A + NEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed, the seed of anise, gives the same flavour as liquorice.

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

parts.note: US means American

explanation.surface: A bookseller offers a pre-owned American printing.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have already been owned before, a synonym.

clue.text: Harrier's first outing? An international and running away with it

parts.note: a test match is an international cricket or rugby match
flight is the act of fleeing

explanation.surface: A runner's debut race: an international meeting, and they flee with the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrier' looks like a cross-country runner but is the jump-jet, whose first outing would be a trial in the air; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A new aircraft's maiden trip aloft is its trial run in the air.

clue.text: Traffic in illegally imported articles is going up

indicators.note: is going up in a down clue says the concealed letters are read from bottom to top
in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across a word join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Smuggled goods are on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took 'in' and 'illegally' with 'Traffic', leaving the hidden word without an indicator; 'in' is that indicator. 'is going up' turns EDART (importED ARTicles) upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to deal in goods, often illicitly, a synonym for commerce.

clue.text: Cross with a male sheep

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Someone is angry with a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Being het up means agitated or annoyed.

clue.text: South African wall-painting incomplete — add one oriental warrior

indicators.note: incomplete means the painting loses its final letter

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A South African mural is left unfinished, and a Japanese fighter is added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last letter of MURAL, leaving MURA.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's feudal military caste, an Eastern warrior.

clue.text: Sailors take their leave if given this freedom

definitions.text: Sailors take their leave if given this
definitions.meaning: a sailor's short shore leave goes by this name

explanation.surface: Sailors go ashore when granted their release.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval shore leave and freedom in general share this word, meaning permission to be at large.

clue.text: Water channel contains gallons, say

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A drain is carrying several gallons, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb UTTER; 'contains' only means the answer is made of these pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter is a trough along a roof or road that carries rainwater away.

clue.text: Ogled, I'd heard, at university

indicators.note: heard says the words I'd are taken by sound, spelt differently

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYED
being up means being in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student at university confesses to having stared.
explanation.walkthrough: I'D said out loud matches EYED; UP is the British sense of being at university, as in 'up at Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone up is to look them over admiringly, an idiom for leering.
